title: Biomolecules
seo_title: Biomolecules Class 12 Chemistry Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 10)
standard_text: Carbohydrates – classification (aldoses and ketoses), monosaccharides (glucose and fructose), D-L configuration, oligosaccharides (sucrose, lactose, maltose), polysaccharides (starch, cellulose, glycogen); importance of carbohydrates. Proteins – elementary idea of amino acids, peptide bond, polypeptides, proteins, structure of proteins – primary, secondary, tertiary structure and quaternary structures (qualitative idea only), denaturation of proteins. Nucleic acids: DNA and RNA. Vitamins – classification and functions.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 10 Biomolecules: carbohydrates, glucose and sugars, amino acids and proteins, protein structure, nucleic acids and vitamins. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids and vitamins are the molecules of life.
key_sub: Sucrose → glucose + fructose; lactose → glucose + galactose.
body_html:
How to think about it

Carbohydrates are monosaccharides (glucose, fructose), disaccharides (sucrose, maltose, lactose) or polysaccharides (starch, cellulose, glycogen). Sucrose is non-reducing; glucose has an aldehyde group and five –OH groups.

Proteins are polymers of amino acids joined by peptide bonds; they have primary, secondary (α-helix, β-sheet), tertiary and quaternary structure and are denatured by heat. Nucleic acids are DNA (deoxyribose, thymine) and RNA (ribose, uracil). Vitamins are fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) or water-soluble (B group, C); lack of each causes a deficiency disease.

Example

Hydrolysis of lactose?

milk sugar

Answer: glucose + galactose

Example

Lack of vitamin C?

bleeding gums

Answer: scurvy

Common mistakes

  • Calling sucrose a reducing sugar.
  • Saying DNA contains uracil.
  • Mixing up fat- and water-soluble vitamins.

faq.q: Why is sucrose a non-reducing sugar?
faq.a: Its glycosidic bond joins the reducing carbons of glucose and fructose, so no free aldehyde or ketone group remains.

faq.q: What happens when a protein is denatured?
faq.a: Its secondary and tertiary structures unfold and it loses its activity, though the peptide bonds remain.
